Hospital Admission History and Physical
Date: 09/08/2026
Patient: Vertie Rutherford, 70-year-old female

Chief Complaint:
Admitted 09/08/2026 for intractable back pain, NRS 10/10 despite IV analgesia.

History of Present Illness:
Vertie Rutherford is a 70-year-old female admitted today due to severe back pain that has not responded to intravenous analgesics. The pain intensity is reported as 10 out of 10 on the numeric rating scale.

Past Medical History:
No additional relevant medical history documented at this time.

Physical Examination:
General: Patient appears in distress due to pain.
Musculoskeletal: Tenderness noted over the lumbar spine region.
Neurological: No focal neurological deficits observed.

Assessment:
Severe intractable back pain requiring hospital admission for pain management and further evaluation.

Plan:
1. Continue pain control measures with close monitoring.
2. Obtain imaging studies to evaluate underlying cause.
3. Consult appropriate specialties as needed.
4. Monitor neurological status regularly.

Summary:
Vertie Rutherford, a 70-year-old female, admitted on 09/08/2026 for intractable back pain, NRS 10/10 despite IV analgesia, requiring comprehensive inpatient management.

notes.author: Radiologist
notes.text:
Radiology Report
Date: 09/04/2026
Patient: Vertie Rutherford, 70-year-old female

Indication:
Evaluation of thoracolumbar spine.

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/04/2026: chronic-appearing L2 compression deformity without bone marrow edema.

No acute fractures or marrow edema identified. The remainder of the thoracic and lumbar vertebrae demonstrate normal marrow signal. No evidence of spinal canal or foraminal stenosis.

Impression:
Chronic L2 compression deformity without signs of acute injury or edema.

notes.title: Spine Intervention Consultation
notes.author: Interventional radiologist
notes.text:
Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/11/2026
Patient: Vertie Rutherford, 70-year-old female

History:
Back pain began 08/22/2026 after a fall from standing height, 3 weeks before this visit. Patient reports localized pain at the site of injury.

Physical Examination:
Back pain localizes to the fractured level; afebrile with no signs of infection or discitis. Neurological examination is unremarkable.

Imaging:
Recent imaging confirms a vertebral compression fracture at the affected level.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Consideration for interventional procedures will be based on further evaluation and patient response.

Summary:
The patient presents with a recent vertebral fracture following a fall. Current management focuses on bone health assessment and education to prevent future fractures.
